fieldMarks: Large, heavy-bodied sea duck: 23-30 in, among the biggest ducks.
Adult male distinctive black-and-white; bill color varies from orange (Alaska) to olive-gray (Northeast).
Female: large, with a long sloping bill and heavy barring on the sides; grayish to rusty brown.
Young males pass through dark-headed, white-chested stages.
behavior: Floats offshore in flocks that can number several thousand; often nests in colonies.
Dives mainly for mussels and other bivalves, also crabs and other invertebrates; often feeds on falling or low tide, by day or night.
Northernmost breeders migrate long distances; southern breeders are more sedentary; Hudson Bay birds stay all year in open leads.
Male courtship calls are a hollow moan and cooing notes; female quacks.
habitat: Stays very close to coastlines in all seasons: rocky coasts and shoals, and in summer islands and coastal tundra.
range: Breeds along northern coasts of Alaska and Canada, including Hudson Bay and the Atlantic coast; the winter range extends only a little south of the breeding range, reaching New England and the Mid-Atlantic.
